title: Glossary
lead: Setting names retain their English spelling so that you can match them to SDK identifiers. This glossary explains abbreviations and how the sample uses them.

rows: API
Application Programming Interface. An interface through which software calls functionality. In this guide, it refers to commands for playback operations and cloud processing.
SDK
Software Development Kit. Development components such as libraries and type definitions integrated into an app. Web, iOS, and Android use different SDKs.
UI
User Interface. The parts users see or operate, such as play buttons, settings menus, and labels.
Config
Short for configuration. PlayerConfig mainly configures the Player, SourceConfig the source, and UIConfig the user interface.
HLS
HTTP Live Streaming. A delivery format that retrieves playlists and media segments over HTTP. It is used for both live and VOD.
DASH
Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP. A delivery format that retrieves media using a manifest called an MPD. Like HLS, it supports both live and VOD.
VOD
Video on Demand. On-demand video for which the viewer can choose when to start and where to seek. The app classifies it using a finite duration.
DVR
Digital Video Recorder. In this app, it means seeking into the available history of a live stream and the rewind window itself.
manifest
A file describing media locations, qualities, tracks, timing, and related information. HLS playlists and DASH MPDs are manifests.
segment
A portion of continuous audio or video divided for delivery. The two-second duration in the media chapter refers to video boundaries; audio segments are not necessarily all the same duration.
ABR
Adaptive Bitrate. Selection of playback quality according to conditions such as network capacity. It is a Player adaptation decision, not a new encode.
AAC
Advanced Audio Coding. An audio compression format. The bundled media uses 48 kHz audio; timing checks account for encoder frames and initial padding.
PTS
Presentation Time Stamp. A media timestamp indicating when to present audio or video. It is usually different from the current wall-clock time.
PDT
Program Date Time. Information mapping media time to a real-world clock. HLS uses fields such as EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME.
QoE
Quality of Experience. A way to assess viewing quality. This app measures startup time, rebuffering, errors, and related events in the browser.
rebuffering
Waiting to accumulate more buffered data after playback has started because data has run short. The app distinguishes it from initial startup waiting and user pauses.
CDN
Content Delivery Network. A network of servers delivering media and other content. Even if a file exists at the origin, caching or referenced-resource availability can affect retrieval.
CORS
Cross-Origin Resource Sharing. A mechanism by which a server permits a Web app from another origin to read a response. An origin is defined by its scheme, host, and port.
DRM
Digital Rights Management. A system for managing rights to view encrypted content. It is separate from the license to use Bitmovin Player itself.
PiP
Picture-in-Picture. Displays video in a separate small window. It differs from casting to another device, such as a TV.
GC
Garbage Collection. Automatic reclamation of memory for unreachable JavaScript objects and similar resources. Its timing varies, and it does not establish that all media memory has been released.
hvc1
An identifier for HEVC video in formats such as MP4. Its presence alone does not guarantee that an OS or browser can decode the video.
RTMP
Real-Time Messaging Protocol. Here it is the input protocol used to send video to a live encoder. The Web Player plays the resulting HLS or DASH.
Per-Title (PerTitle)
An encoding method that analyzes each video to choose resolution and bitrate combinations. It operates at a different stage from ABR during playback.
Bundle ID (BundleID)
An Apple application identifier used when allowing an app on a license. The corresponding Android identifier is applicationId; it is a different setting.
